What is an Expert Advisor (EA) in gold and forex trading?

An Expert Advisor (EA) is a MetaTrader program that can analyse prices and, with trading permission, send orders. Gold and forex examples show how signals, fills and account records differ.

Research guide3 min readPublished by Surfer Quant
01

From a strategy rule to an order

A gold price can briefly cross a level and close below it. A rule triggered on a touch and one triggered on a close can therefore produce different signals. Check the instrument, timeframe and trigger before looking at the order and exit rules.

02

Why a signal and a fill can differ

The price shown on a forex chart can differ from the price available for an order. To trace a trade, compare the program log, order status and fill price in time order, alongside the spread and trading session.

03

Which version and records to compare

When comparing two EAs, record the version, instruments, settings and test period. Backtests use historical data and demo fills can differ from live fills. Check the cost assumptions and whether drawdown uses balance or equity including open positions.

This is a general guide to strategy evaluation and operations, not individualized investment advice.
